tone_statements.citation: Manifi Abouh, Maxime Yves Julien & Etienne Sadembouo. 2014. De la dénomination des concepts techniques dans l'élaboration d'un lexique thématique agricole bilingue français-yambetta [Designing technical concepts in the elaboration of a thematic bilingual French/Yambeta agricultural lexicon]. In: TALAf 2014 : Traitement Automatique des Langues Africaines (atelier de TALN-RECITAL 2014, Marseille), pp. 159-171. ACL Anthology W14-6507.
tone_statements.quote: Alors, les lexèmes empruntés étaient simplement adaptés à la phonologie du yambetta. Autrement dit, il fallait se conformer aux contraintes phonémique, syllabique et prosodique de cette langue ; et manifestement, comme la plupart des langues africaines en général et bantoues en particulier, le yambetta est une langue à tons et n'admet pas de suite consonantique.
tone_statements.translation: So the borrowed lexemes were simply adapted to the phonology of Yambetta. In other words, one had to conform to the phonemic, syllabic and prosodic constraints of this language; and manifestly, like most African languages in general and Bantu languages in particular, Yambetta is a tone language and does not admit consonant sequences.

sources.citation: Koung, Eric. 2024. Le verbe en yambɛta : de la description à l'enseignement. Mémoire de Master, Université de Yaoundé I (FALSH). 162 pp. DICAMES hdl 20.500.12177/13388.
sources.note: No word-stress statement. Sec. 1.5 'Les marques tonales en yambeta' p. 20: two level tones H and L, every syllable bears H or L, contour tones = sequences on adjacent vowels; only H marked in orthography (after Phillips 1979:107). P. 9 uses 'accentuée'/'accent sur la première syllabe' loosely for what it itself calls a 'variation tonale' in an etymology anecdote (tɛmɛn vs tɛmɛnan) -- not a stress rule.

sources.citation: Boyd, Virginia Lee (Ginger). 2015. The phonological systems of the Mbam languages of Cameroon with a focus on vowels and vowel harmony. PhD dissertation, Universiteit Leiden. LOT Dissertation Series 410. Utrecht: LOT. xviii+413 pp. (sec. 2.3 'Yambeta phonological overview' pp. 61-82, Nigii dialect)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.3.5 Tone (p. 80-82): 'Yambeta has a two-tone system underlyingly, high and low. Rising tones and falling tones occur only due to glide formation from syllable mergers.' Noun-root melodies H/L/HL/LH, verb-root melodies L/LH/H, grammatical tone in TAM; long vowels restricted to the first root syllable (p. 66). The words stress/accent occur nowhere in the Yambeta sections (only a Dixon & Aikhenvald definition on p. 257).

sources.note: Terminology paper, not a phonology; the whole text was searched for ton/tons/tonal/tonologie/prosodique and the single hit read in context: in sec. 4.2.4 'L'emprunt' (loanword adaptation) the authors state first-hand that borrowed lexemes must conform to the phonemic, syllabic and prosodic constraints of Yambetta, which 'est une langue à tons' and admits no consonant sequences. No tone inventory, no tone rules; Yambetta examples are printed in a legacy SIL font with tone diacritics.
